contradiction_branches.conflict_target: closedness of reflection positivity under the selected cutoff-removal topology
contradiction_branches.contradiction_carrier: a negative reflection-positivity quadratic form in the limiting gauge-invariant Schwinger functions
contradiction_branches.derived_consequence: If the negative continuum form exists while all approximating reflection forms are nonnegative and the cone is closed, the limit would both belong and not belong to the OS-positive cone.
contradiction_branches.exact_negation: There exists a finite reflected test-observable family f_i and coefficients c_i such that the continuum reflection form sum_i,j conjugate(c_i)c_j S(Theta f_i,f_j) is strictly negative.
failure_modes: The limiting topology is too weak to preserve the reflection form.
The test-observable family changes across the cutoff sequence.
Gauge fixing or quotienting changes the observable sector.
contradiction_branches.learning_if_failed: Failure would show that the continuum route needs a sharper topology or a different construction of the OS-positive sector before spectral reasoning can be trusted.
preserved_commitments: The regulated approximants are reflection-positive in the same gauge-invariant observable sector.
The limiting topology is strong enough for the reflection form to be a closed nonnegative cone.
The limiting Schwinger functions are the same objects used for reconstruction and later gap analysis.
proof_obligations: Specify the topology on gauge-invariant Schwinger distributions.
Prove reflection positivity is closed in that topology for the chosen observable algebra.
Show the negative test family survives the OS null-vector quotient.

contradiction_branches.conflict_target: same-theory non-Gaussian or nonzero connected-cumulant witness
contradiction_branches.contradiction_carrier: a connected gauge-invariant cumulant or Wilson-loop observable in the same limiting Schwinger family
contradiction_branches.derived_consequence: The assumed trivial collapse forces the selected connected cumulant to vanish, while the same-theory witness requires a nonzero interacting cumulant in that limit.
contradiction_branches.exact_negation: Every continuum subsequential limit of the regulated gauge-invariant Yang-Mills observables is Gaussian/free or has vanishing connected cumulants for the nontriviality witness family.
failure_modes: The witness comes from a different approximation scheme.
The cumulant normalization vanishes or diverges in the limit.
The branch proves only non-Gaussianity at finite cutoff.
contradiction_branches.learning_if_failed: Failure would demote the route to a nontriviality-evidence task rather than allowing the gap analysis to proceed on an empty continuum theory.
preserved_commitments: The nontriviality witness is measured in the same limiting Schwinger functions S_n.
Connected cumulants are defined after the same cutoff-removal process as OS reconstruction.
Gauge invariance and Euclidean covariance remain active commitments.
proof_obligations: Select the witness observable family and its normalization.
Prove the witness belongs to the same continuum object as the OS reconstruction.
Show the witness distinguishes interacting Yang-Mills from a Gaussian/free limit.

Same-theory invariant means construction, reconstruction, nontriviality, and gap witnesses refer to the same limiting object S_n.

packets.lemma_statement: For compact simple gauge group G on four-dimensional Euclidean space, suppose a directed family of regulated Yang-Mills measures or Schwinger distributions has Balaban-style multiscale effective-action bounds strong enough to give tightness/convergence on gauge-invariant observables, and suppose reflection positivity, Euclidean covariance, gauge invariance, and a non-Gaussian observable witness are preserved uniformly through cutoff removal. Then a subsequential continuum family of gauge-invariant Schwinger functions S_n exists, is OS-positive, is nontrivial, and reconstructs a candidate physical Hilbert space H_YM with vacuum Omega and time-translation semigroup.
next_recursive_subgoals: Search the KB/prior-art cache for the strongest Balaban precompactness or convergence statement.
Choose the limiting topology and state the closure lemma for reflection positivity.
Select a candidate gauge-invariant nontriviality observable.

Attach one non-Gaussian gauge-invariant observable witness to rule out triviality.
Record the reconstructed H_YM, Omega, and semigroup as outputs of S_n, not as independent postulates.

assumptions: OS reconstruction identifies Euclidean time translation with exp(-tH) on H_YM.
The observable family is dense in the physical vacuum-orthogonal sector after quotienting OS null vectors.
The connected correlation decay rate m satisfies liminf m_{a,L} >= m0 > 0.

contradiction_branches.conflict_target: spectral support exclusion E_H((0,m0))P_perp = 0 obtained from OS reconstruction, density, and uniform Euclidean decay
contradiction_branches.contradiction_carrier: low-energy vacuum-orthogonal spectral measures or observable-generated approximants in the reconstructed H_YM
contradiction_branches.derived_consequence: The no-gap assumption puts spectral mass arbitrarily close to zero, while a spectrally determining observable family with cutoff-uniform e^{-m0 t} decay forces its spectral measures to have no support in (0,m0).
contradiction_branches.exact_negation: For every epsilon > 0 there exists psi_epsilon in P_perp H_YM with ||psi_epsilon|| = 1 and <psi_epsilon,H psi_epsilon> < epsilon; equivalently the vacuum-orthogonal spectral support of H meets (0,epsilon) for arbitrarily small epsilon.
failure_modes: The no-gap vectors live outside the observable-generated sector.
The decay estimate is finite-cutoff, strong-coupling, or not uniform in the continuum limit.
The route silently changes from the reconstructed H_YM to a different Hamiltonian or subsequence.
contradiction_branches.learning_if_failed: Failure would identify whether the next pivot should attack observable density, uniform decay, or same-theory reconstruction rather than continuing a generic mass-gap slogan.
preserved_commitments: H, Omega, and P_perp are reconstructed from the same OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions.
Gauge-invariant vacuum-subtracted observables are dense in P_perp H_YM.
The Euclidean connected two-point decay bound holds uniformly with rate bounded below by m0 > 0.
proof_obligations: Prove the gauge-invariant observable family is dense in the physical vacuum-orthogonal sector.
Show the low-energy vectors can be approximated by vacuum-subtracted observable vectors.
Prove the Laplace-transform spectral support lemma for the reconstructed Hamiltonian.
Transport the cutoff-uniform decay estimate to the continuum without changing the object.

definitions: Spectrally determining means the closure of vacuum-subtracted gauge-invariant observable vectors is P_perp H_YM.
Cutoff-uniform means the decay rate has a positive lower bound before taking the continuum limit.
P_perp is the projection away from the reconstructed vacuum sector, not a regulator-level excitation space.

equations.valid_when: The constants are controlled uniformly for the same observable family that survives reconstruction.

equations.label: Hamiltonian gap conclusion
equations.valid_when: The observable family is spectrally determining, so decay support restrictions extend from A Omega vectors to P_perp H_YM.

failure_tests: Reject if the decay is only a strong-coupling or finite-lattice estimate.

Reject if the continuum construction and spectral estimate refer to different limiting objects.
packets.lemma_statement: Suppose the same OS-positive continuum Yang-Mills Schwinger functions S_n reconstruct H_YM, Omega, H and a gauge-invariant observable algebra A_ginv. If a spectrally determining vacuum-subtracted family A in A_ginv has connected Euclidean time correlations bounded by C_A exp(-m t) with m >= m0 > 0 uniformly through cutoff removal, then the reconstructed Hamiltonian has no vacuum-orthogonal spectrum in (0,m0), hence Spec(H restricted to P_perp H_YM) subset [m0,infinity).
